description:
Evidence: docs/research/handwired.md, stage 2 and stage 1b. A sparse layer with a gather per term (bench/handwired_f32.exs, kernel layer32) takes 0.378 us per item, 5.5x the hand-written C float loop (0.069 us). The generated C of each term has: a bounds-checked [f32] read with a finite check (defk_get_f32, defk_in_f64), two overflow-checked i64 index operations (defk_mul_i64, defk_add_i64 on r * k + t and base + idx), a bounds-checked [i32] read, a checked float multiply, a non-finite check on the add, and a range check on each [f32] store (defk_to_f32). The stage 1b NFA kernel (bench/handwired_classes.exs) has 17 context-taking helper calls per byte for 3.2 ns per byte; several operate on values that are provably 0 or 1 (band/bsr results, hit * (1 - ext)).
Defk.Facts already has range rules for band (bit_facts/3); what remains unproven is not measured.

Steps:
1. Dump the C and read the fast-path report (Defk.Report) for the two kernels; list every check that remains in the hot loop, per statement.
2. For each, name the fact that would remove it and say whether ADR-0007's representation can state it (for example: band(x, 1) is 0..1, so a product with it cannot overflow; loop bounds bound r * k + t; an [i32] element is in i32 range so base + idx cannot overflow i64).
3. Implement the cheapest proofs only. Semantics must not change: the byte-identical gate (mix dump_c, docs/agents/runs.md) must show a diff only in kernels that gain a proof; unit tests of the area; Elixir mode agreement unchanged.
4. Measure the two scripts once on a quiet machine, before and after (ps quiet test), and record the table of checks (removed, why not) and the us per item in docs/performance.md.
Rules: run what the change touches (docs/agents/runs.md); no sweeping benches. Done when the table of checks and the before/after numbers are recorded, or a closed-as-not-possible comment says which check blocks each proof.
title: Gather loops: find which runtime checks Defk.Facts could prove away (f32 layer is 5.5x slower than C float)
